name: Al-Hudud al-Khamsa (The Five Cosmic Luminaries)
note: Collective hub: the five cosmic ranks (al-hudud al-ulwiyya) through which the divine unity is mediated in Druze cosmology; attested in Abu-Izzeddin and standard scholarship.

name: Al-Aql al-Kulli (the Universal Intellect)
note: First and highest of the five luminaries, the Universal Intellect; held to be manifested in Hamza ibn Ali. Attested doctrine.

name: Al-Nafs al-Kulliyya (the Universal Soul)
note: Second luminary, the Universal Soul, emanating from the Intellect; associated with Abu Ibrahim Isma'il al-Tamimi.

name: Al-Kalima (the Word)
note: Third luminary, the Word/Logos; associated with Muhammad ibn Wahb al-Tamimi. Attested.

name: Al-Sabiq (the Preceder / Right Wing)
note: Fourth luminary, the Preceder (also 'the Right Wing'); associated with Salama ibn Abd al-Wahhab. Attested.

name: Al-Tali (the Follower / Left Wing)
note: Fifth luminary, the Follower (also 'the Left Wing'); associated with Baha al-Din al-Muqtana. Attested.

name: Hamza ibn Ali ibn Ahmad
note: Persian founder-theologian of the Druze daʿwa (fl. 1017-21); chief organizer, held as the human manifestation of al-Aql (Universal Intellect). Historically attested. HOMONYM: distinct from ENT_ISL_HAMZA (Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, uncle of the Prophet Muhammad).

name: Abu Ibrahim Isma'il al-Tamimi
note: Early Druze daʿi associated with the rank of al-Nafs (Universal Soul). Attested in Druze epistolary tradition.

name: Muhammad ibn Wahb al-Qurashi al-Tamimi
note: Early Druze daʿi associated with the rank of al-Kalima (the Word). HOMONYM: distinct from the Prophet Muhammad (ENT_ISL_MUHAMMAD).

name: Salama ibn Abd al-Wahhab
note: Early Druze daʿi associated with the rank of al-Sabiq (the Preceder). Attested.

name: Baha al-Din al-Muqtana al-Samuqi
note: Druze daʿi (fl. 1027-43) who compiled much of the Rasaʾil al-Hikma (Epistles of Wisdom) and sealed the daʿwa; held as the manifestation of al-Tali (the Follower). Attested.

name: Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah
note: Sixth Fatimid caliph-imam (r.996-1021); in Druze belief the manifestation (mazhar/tajalli) of the divine unity. Historically attested Fatimid ruler; his divinity is a confessional Druze claim, modeled descriptively.

name: Muhammad al-Darazi (Nashtakin al-Darazi)
note: Early daʿi (d. c.1018) whose extremist preaching gave the community its exonym 'Druze'; later repudiated by Hamza as a heretic. Historically attested.

name: Taqammus (transmigration of souls)
note: Druze doctrine that the fixed number of souls transmigrate immediately from body to body (taqammus); a defining publicly attested tenet.

name: Tawhid (the Druze doctrine of divine unity)
note: The unitarian core from which the Druze self-designation Muwahhidun ('Unitarians') derives; God beyond attributes, mediated through the hudud. Attested.

name: Rasaʾil al-Hikma (Epistles of Wisdom)
note: The 111-epistle Druze sacred canon, largely by Hamza and al-Muqtana; foundational closed scripture. Existence and authorship attested in scholarship.
